title: Popover
summary: A floating panel anchored to a control is the SwiftUI popover. With presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover) it stays a popover on a phone instead of becoming a sheet. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a small amount of interactive content that belongs to one control: a filter panel, a quick edit, a short explanation with a link.
whenNotToUse: Not for a list of actions (use Menu), not for text that only names a control (use help and an accessibility hint), and not for a task with several steps or a keyboard-heavy form on a phone (use sheet).
api: func popover<Content: View>(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, attachmentAnchor: PopoverAttachmentAnchor = .rect(.bounds), arrowEdge: Edge? = nil, content: @escaping () -> Content) -> some View
func presentationCompactAdaptation(_ adaptation: PresentationAdaptation) -> some View
func presentationBackground<S: ShapeStyle>(_ style: S) -> some View

states.name: open
states.description: The system draws the panel with an arrow pointing at the anchor. A tap outside closes it.

states.name: adapted
states.description: Without presentationCompactAdaptation the popover becomes a sheet at compact width.

appearance: The system draws the panel, its arrow and its shadow in every theme. presentationBackground with the theme's raised background colour makes the panel match Monarch surfaces; the content uses Monarch components.
platformNotes: The web Popover is non-modal: the page behind stays interactive. An iOS popover takes the first tap outside to dismiss itself, so the content behind it cannot be used while it is open. The web's side and align are arrowEdge and attachmentAnchor; the system moves the panel when there is no room. The web's PopoverClose is a button that sets isPresented to false. Android builds a MonarchPopover because Compose has no anchored panel with an arrow; iOS has one, so nothing is built here.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver focus moves into the popover when it opens and is confined to it; the escape gesture closes it and focus returns to the anchor.
The popover has no title of its own; start the content with a heading, marked with accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader).
Give the popover a way to close that is not a tap outside when it contains a form: a Done button.
edgeCases: The popover sizes itself to its content. Give long text a width with frame(idealWidth:) so it wraps instead of growing across the screen.
At the largest text sizes the content may be taller than the screen; put it in a ScrollView.
Without presentationCompactAdaptation the same code shows a sheet on a phone, so test both widths.

examples.title: Filters
examples.template:
MonarchButton({{trigger}}) { isShown = true }
    .popover(isPresented: $isShown, arrowEdge: .top) {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: theme.spacing.space3) {
            Toggle({{options.0.label}}, isOn: $first)
                .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox)
                .monarchTextStyle(.body)
            Toggle({{options.1.label}}, isOn: $second)
                .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox)
                .monarchTextStyle(.body)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textDefault)
        .padding(theme.spacing.space4)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
        .accessibilityLabel({{label}})
        .presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover)
        .presentationBackground(theme.colors.bgRaised)
    }
examples.code:
MonarchButton("Filters") { isShown = true }
    .popover(isPresented: $isShown, arrowEdge: .top) {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: theme.spacing.space3) {
            Toggle("Only mine", isOn: $first)
                .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox)
                .monarchTextStyle(.body)
            Toggle("Unassigned", isOn: $second)
                .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox)
                .monarchTextStyle(.body)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textDefault)
        .padding(theme.spacing.space4)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
        .accessibilityLabel("Filters")
        .presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover)
        .presentationBackground(theme.colors.bgRaised)
    }
